title: Mirai_Botnet_Investigation_813
description: Investigate and identify the source of unusual traffic patterns and performance degradation in the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and performance degradation. Your task is to investigate and identify the source of the problem. Learning objective: Investigate a Mirai botnet infection by identifying suspicious systemd service unit names, abnormal network traffic, and persistence mechanisms.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.
levels.solution: Check the running services and look for any unusual or unfamiliar services. Pay attention to services that might be communicating with external hosts. The flag you are looking for is a systemd service unit name named 'bot-beacon.service'.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Start by listing all running services on the system.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system installation or are unfamiliar.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-timers --all' to list all systemd timers and look for 'bot-beacon.timer'.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Network Traffic
levels.content: Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.
levels.solution: Investigate the network connections and look for any services that are sending a high volume of traffic to an external host. The flag you are looking for is a systemd service unit name named 'bot-flood.service'.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Monitor network connections to identify services sending high volumes of traffic.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use network monitoring tools to identify services communicating with external hosts.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the command 'ss -tulnp' to list all network connections and look for 'bot-flood.timer'.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.
levels.solution: Check the systemd services and timers to identify how the suspicious service is being started automatically. The flag you are looking for is a systemd service unit name named 'system-update-checker.service'.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Investigate how services are set to start automatically after a system reboot.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for systemd timers that might be triggering the suspicious service.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-dependencies --after system-update-checker.timer' to check dependencies and look for 'system-update-checker.timer'.
